# Psalm 78 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A contemplative poem of Asaph. My people, listen to what I'm about to teach you. Open your ears to what I have to say.

**2** I'm going to tell you an ancient story — I'll reveal lessons hidden since the beginning.

**3** These are things we've heard and known, things our ancestors passed down to us.

**4** We will not keep them secret from our children. We'll tell the next generation about the LORD's praiseworthy deeds, his power, and the amazing things he's done.

**5** He established his law for Jacob's descendants and gave his instructions to Israel, commanding our ancestors to teach them to their children,

**6** so that the next generation would learn them — even children not yet born — and they in turn would teach their own children.

**7** Then they would put their confidence in God, never forget what God has done, and obey his commands.

**8** They would not be like their ancestors — a stubborn, rebellious generation whose hearts weren't loyal and whose spirits couldn't be trusted with God.

**9** The warriors of Ephraim, armed with bows, turned and ran on the day of battle.

**10** They didn't honor their covenant with God and refused to live by his instructions.

**11** They forgot what he'd done — the wonders he'd shown them.

**12** He performed miracles right in front of their ancestors, in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.

**13** He split the sea and brought them through; he made the water stand up like walls.

**14** He guided them with a cloud by day and lit their way with fire all night long.

**15** He cracked open rocks in the desert and gave them water as plentiful as the ocean depths.

**16** He made streams pour out of solid rock — water flowed like rivers!

**17** But they just kept on sinning against him, defying the Most High in that barren land.

**18** They deliberately tested God by demanding the food they were craving.

**19** They challenged God, saying, 'Can God really set a dinner table out here in the wilderness?'

**20** 'Sure, he struck the rock and water came pouring out. But can he give us bread too? Can he supply meat for all his people?'

**21** When the LORD heard this, he burned with anger. His fury blazed against Jacob; his wrath flared against Israel,

**22** because they didn't believe God and didn't trust him to take care of them.

**23** Yet he gave orders to the sky above and threw open heaven's doors.

**24** He rained down manna for them to eat — actual grain from heaven!

**25** People ate the bread of angels; he sent them more food than they could handle.

**26** He unleashed the east wind from the sky and drove the south wind with his power.

**27** He rained meat on them thick as dust — birds as countless as grains of sand on the shore.

**28** He dropped them right in the middle of the camp, all around their tents.

**29** They ate and stuffed themselves; he gave them exactly what they wanted.

**30** But before they'd even finished eating, while the food was literally still in their mouths,

**31** God's anger exploded against them. He struck down their strongest and cut down Israel's finest young men.

**32** Even after all this, they kept sinning. Despite miracle after miracle, they still wouldn't trust him.

**33** So he let their days fade away like a puff of air, and their years ended in sudden disaster.

**34** Whenever he struck them down, suddenly they went looking for him — they turned back and desperately searched for God.

**35** They remembered that God was their rock, that God Most High was their rescuer.

**36** But they were just flattering him with their words — lying through their teeth.

**37** Their hearts weren't really in it. They weren't faithful to his covenant.

**38** Yet God was merciful. He forgave their sin and didn't destroy them. Time and again he held back his anger and didn't unleash his full fury.

**39** He remembered that they were only human — here today and gone like a gust of wind.

**40** How many times they rebelled against him in the wilderness! How often they caused him pain in that wasteland!

**41** Again and again they tested God and pushed the Holy One of Israel to the limit.

**42** They didn't remember his power — the day he rescued them from the enemy,

**43** when he displayed his miraculous signs in Egypt, his wonders in the region of Zoan.

**44** He turned their rivers into blood so no one could drink from them.

**45** He sent swarms of flies that ate them alive and frogs that overran everything.

**46** He handed their crops over to grasshoppers and the fruit of all their work to locusts.

**47** He demolished their grapevines with hail and shattered their fig trees with sleet.

**48** He pounded their cattle with hail and their livestock with bolts of lightning.

**49** He unleashed his blazing anger on them — fury, rage, and trouble — a whole army of destroying angels.

**50** He cleared a highway for his anger. He didn't spare them from death but handed their lives over to the plague.

**51** He struck down every firstborn in Egypt — the pride and firstfruits of every family in the land of Ham.

**52** Then he led his own people out like sheep and guided them through the desert like a flock.

**53** He led them to safety — they had nothing to fear — while the sea swallowed their enemies whole.

**54** He brought them to his holy land, to the mountain his own power had won.

**55** He drove the nations out ahead of them, divided the land among them as their inheritance, and settled Israel's tribes in their new homes.

**56** But they tested and defied God Most High and wouldn't obey his commands.

**57** They turned their backs and betrayed him, just like their ancestors. They were as unreliable as a warped bow.

**58** They infuriated him with their pagan worship sites and made him jealous with their carved idols.

**59** God heard it all and burned with anger. He completely rejected Israel.

**60** He abandoned his home at Shiloh — the tent where he'd lived among his people.

**61** He let the Ark — his power and glory — be captured by the enemy.

**62** He handed his people over to the sword; he was furious with his own inheritance.

**63** Fire devoured their young men, and their young women had no one to marry.

**64** Their priests were cut down by the sword, and their widows couldn't even grieve.

**65** Then the Lord snapped awake like someone waking from sleep — like a warrior shaking off the effects of wine.

**66** He drove back his enemies and put them to lasting shame.

**67** He rejected Joseph's family line and didn't choose the tribe of Ephraim.

**68** Instead he chose Judah's tribe and Mount Zion, the place he loves.

**69** He built his sanctuary as permanent as the heavens, as enduring as the earth he established forever.

**70** He chose David his servant and pulled him away from the sheep pens.

**71** He took him from tending the ewes and their lambs to be the shepherd of Jacob, his people — Israel, his special possession.

**72** And David led them with an honest heart and guided them with skilled hands.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **78:1-4**: This is the Bible's longest history lesson — 72 verses of 'don't repeat our mistakes.' The emphasis on telling children is striking: faith survives only through intentional storytelling.

- **78:36-39**: The most heartbreaking cycle: they flattered God with their lips while lying with their tongues. And yet — 'he was merciful.' God's patience outlasts human fickleness.

- **78:70-72**: The ending is beautiful: after 72 verses of failure, God picks a shepherd boy. David doesn't represent Israel getting its act together — he represents God's grace starting fresh.

— PNEUMA
